nearest: st.sidewalk ('area for pedestrians between roadway and property line'): the area between a bicycle lane and the sidewalk is no sidewalk and its passability is not carried; st.obstruction is an object, not an impassable area

span: to disobey the instructions of any official traffic-control device
proposal: `compliesWithDeviceRules (subject)`: true at an observation where every rule of the set that states the instruction an official traffic-control device gives the road user it governs, and is engaged for the subject there, is complied with; false where one such engaged rule is violated; unknown otherwise. It decides the action the law requires: what the device governing the road user instructs it to do, which the words leave to the instruction of whatever device governs, naming no rule.
nearest: Formula.rule (composes one named rule; the words name none, only 'the instructions of any' device); dev.traffic_signal, dev.stop_sign, dev.yield_sign, dev.regulatory_sign, dev.lane_control_signal (each carries a device's state or code, and dev.regulatory_sign is 'not a stand-in for a manoeuvre': none carries the conduct the device instructs)

span: when transporting pupils to and from school.
proposal: `ru.pupil_transport_service` | a school bus is on a trip carrying pupils to or from a school or a school activity, as the source records the bus's service state (its operator's dispatch record, or a displayed route or destination). **Not a stand-in for:** the number of occupants (`ru.occupant_count`) — a bus may carry persons who are not pupils, or travel empty on a pupil route | local
nearest: ru.occupant_count ('the number of persons in or on a vehicle': it counts persons, it does not tell pupils from other passengers nor a school trip from another); ru.school_bus (the bus's designation and markings, which it carries whether or not it transports pupils)

span: This section shall not apply to the driver of any vehicle which is disabled while on the paved or main-traveled portion of a highway in such manner and to such extent that it is impossible to avoid stopping and temporarily leaving such disabled vehicle in such position.
proposal: `ru.disabled` | the vehicle cannot move under its own power (a breakdown, damage, a flat tyre), as the source records it **Not a stand-in for:** a vehicle at rest with its engine stopped, or one showing hazard lamps -- the condition is not a halt and not a signal | general
nearest: kin.engine_running (Not a stand-in for: motion or a halt -- a vehicle stands with its engine running and rolls with it stopped; an engine off is not a vehicle unable to move); sig.hazard (a signal a road user emits, not the vehicle's condition)

span: or in compliance with law
proposal: `compliesWithEngaged` (Formula.compliesWithEngaged (binder map)): an operator that decides whether, at an observation, the subject's present conduct is required by some rule of the accepted set that is engaged for the subject there and is complied with by that conduct, so that a halt 'in compliance with law' is a halt some engaged rule requires of the subject (a stop at a sign, a yield to oncoming traffic or to an emergency vehicle, a stop for a school bus); it decides the time and the reason of the halt the law excuses
nearest: dev.governs, dev.stop_sign, dev.traffic_signal, rel.occupies, st.travel_region read only the halts a governing device requires; Formula.rule and Formula.ruleApplies compose one named rule each, never 'law' as the set of all rules engaged for the subject

span: Within 50 feet of the nearest rail of a railroad.
proposal: | `st.railway_track` | the rails of a railway wherever they run on or beside a highway, crossing the roadway or not, each rail a region with a boundary so that the ground distance from a road user to the nearest rail is read through `st.region_geometry`; **kind** ∈ {railroad, streetcar}, a streetcar line being one whose cars run on the street **Not a stand-in for:** the level crossing as a place (`st.railway_crossing`) | general |
nearest: st.railway_crossing ("level crossing of a railway with the roadway, and its nearest rail"): it carries rails only where a railway crosses the roadway, so the distance to a railroad's rails that run beside a highway is read by no atom, and it does not tell a railroad from a streetcar line, which the railroad definition excludes; st.region_geometry measures only to regions the ontology names. The distinction decided: where the halt is forbidden (within the distance of a railroad's nearest rail).

span: shall not stop, stand or park a vehicle other than at the angle to the curb or edge of the highway indicated by such devices.
proposal: Term.cosDeg (a : Term) : the cosine of an angle a given in degrees, a ratio; unknown where a is unknown. It decides where the act is required: whether a vehicle stands at the angle the devices indicate, by comparing the cosine of its angle to the curb (the dot product of kin.heading with the curb-side carrier's st.lane_direction) with the cosine of the bay's angle (st.parking_space angle, deg).
nearest: kin.heading and st.lane_direction give the cosine of the vehicle's angle to the curb; st.parking_space gives the indicated angle in degrees; no Term relates the two (no trigonometric operator), and an approximation by a table of literal angles would be a model the words do not state.

span: lawfully
proposal: Formula.compliesWithEngaged (who : Arg) (conduct : String) : at the observation, every rule of the set that governs conduct of the named kind (here standing or parking) and is engaged for road user who is complied with. It decides which road users the duty concerns: a vehicle lawfully parked, as against one parked against any parking rule (the same need as gap smoke31-1111-0039:G22 for 'in compliance with law').
nearest: dev.regulatory_sign, dev.governs, rel.occupies, st.travel_region: a posted prohibition governing the vehicle's place is one ground of unlawful parking among many (distances from hydrants, crosswalks, curbs; durations), so its absence is not lawfulness; Formula.rule composes one named rule only, and the words name none.

span: in such position as to block the driveway or entrance to any abutting property.
proposal: `st.property_entrance` | a driveway, private road or other entrance by which abutting property is entered from a highway or an alley, at the place where it meets that way **Not a stand-in for:** the junction of an alley or a public way with another way | general — it decides where a halt is forbidden: across the access to a property, as against at the alley's own mouth onto a street.
nearest: st.driveway_or_alley_entrance: 'Not a stand-in for: which of them meets the highway there — the kind does not tell an alley's entrance from a private road's or driveway's'; inside an alley it marks the alley's own junction as well as a property's driveway.

span: use alternate routes whenever possible.
proposal: `st.alternate_route` | relation: for a road user on a controlled-access highway, a way of the road network other than a controlled-access highway, open to the road user's class, that connects the place at which the road user entered that highway with the place at which it leaves it, as the map's routing records; true where such a way exists **Not a stand-in for:** the road user's destination or plan, nor a road's speed, capacity or congestion | general
nearest: rel.occupies, st.controlled_access: they show the road user is on a controlled-access highway and so not on an alternate route, but not whether an alternate route to the same place exists, which decides whether the duty to use one can be carried out ('whenever possible').

span: shall give all signals by hand and arm in the manner required
proposal: `sig.hand_signal_posture` | the posture of a driver's or rider's arm signal: **arm** in {left, right}, the arm extended; **side** in {left, right}, the side of the vehicle or device beyond which it is extended; **direction** in {horizontal, upward, downward}, the direction the hand and arm point **Not a stand-in for:** the meaning of the signal (`sig.hand_signal`), which a source may decode from different postures | general
nearest: sig.hand_signal: its contract carries 'the meaning of the one given' only, not the arm, side or direction of the extension, which is the manner the duty requires (the action the law requires: which arm and which direction).

span: except that the operator may give a signal for a right turn by extending his or her right hand and arm horizontally and to the right side of the bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter.
proposal: `sig.hand_signal_posture` | the posture of a driver's or rider's arm signal: **arm** in {left, right}, the arm extended; **side** in {left, right}, the side of the vehicle or device beyond which it is extended; **direction** in {horizontal, upward, downward}, the direction the hand and arm point **Not a stand-in for:** the meaning of the signal (`sig.hand_signal`), which a source may decode from different postures | general
nearest: sig.hand_signal: meaning 'right' is the same for the right arm extended horizontally to the right and the left arm extended upward; the exception turns on which posture is used, which its contract does not carry.

span: any unprotected hose
proposal: `st.protected_hose` | a hose lying on or across a way that a hose bridge or ramp covers, so that a vehicle crossing it does not bear on the hose; a region with a boundary, coinciding with the covered stretch of an `st.obstruction` of kind hose **Not a stand-in for:** a bare hose (`st.obstruction` kind hose without this cover), or a barrier | general
nearest: st.obstruction kind hose: its contract records 'a physical object on or beside the roadway that is not a road user' and its kind, not whether the hose is protected; whether driving over it is forbidden turns on that distinction (the action the law forbids).

span: without the consent of the fire department official in command.
proposal: `dev.fire_official_direction` | the fire department official in command at a fire scene directing road users, and the direction given; **indication** in {stop, proceed}, with `dev.governs` relating it to the travel regions it controls **Not a stand-in for:** a police officer's, flagger's or crossing guard's direction (`dev.human_direction`) | general
nearest: dev.human_direction: its role attribute is one of {police_officer, flagger, school_crossing_guard, railroad_flagger}; the consent of 'the fire department official in command', which decides whether the vehicle may drive over the hose, is none of them.

span: (c) When directed by an official traffic control device.
proposal: `dev.lamps_on_sign` | a regulatory sign directing road users to display lighted lamps (headlamps on) where it governs, with `dev.governs` relating it to the travel regions it controls and the same structured **conditions** attribute as `dev.zone_sign` **Not a stand-in for:** whether lamps are lit (`sig.headlamp`) or whether it is dark (`env.darkness`) | general
nearest: dev.regulatory_sign: its catalogue of codes has no lamps-on direction; dev.zone_sign: its kinds include no headlight zone; whether the device directs lamps on decides when the display is required (the time of the duty).

span: during the times specified in
proposal: | `dev.lamps_on_sign` | an official sign or device directing road users to display lighted lamps (headlamps on) where it governs, the stretch it governs read through `dev.governs` | general |
nearest: dev.regulatory_sign: 'a point regulation by catalogue code' whose closed code list (no_left_turn ... no_trucks) holds no code directing the display of lamps; dev.zone_sign: its kinds (school ... trail) name no lamps-on zone. Whether lamps are required on the stretch the subject drives (the time of the duty) is the distinction no atom decides; the same gap is pending as smoke31-1111-0039:G21 on NRS-484D-100-1.
